item.description: According to a report by The Balochistan Post, ten people, including a student, were allegedly forcibly disappeared across Balochistan, while four missing men were recovered in Kech. Meanwhile, the ...
item.content:encoded:
Ten people, including 15-year-old student, allegedly disappear in Balochistan; four missing men recovered According to a report by The Balochistan Post, ten people, including a student, were allegedly forcibly disappeared across Balochistan, while four missing men were recovered in Kech. Meanwhile, the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons continued its long-running protest in Quetta, demanding constitutional accountability, transparency, and the safe return of detainees. ANI | Updated: 05-11-2026 14:49 IST | Created: 05-11-2026 14:49 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Ten people, including a 15-year-old student, have allegedly been forcibly disappeared in separate incidents across Balochistan, while four previously missing men have reportedly been recovered in the province's Kech district, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP). Citing local sources, TBP reported that four of the alleged disappearance cases were recorded in Quetta, the provincial capital. Sources accused personnel of Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Military Intelligence (MI) and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) of involvement in the disappearances. Meanwhile, four men who had allegedly been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces in Kech district were recovered in Turbat between October 25 and 28, the report said. The report also highlighted the ongoing protest by the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) outside the Quetta Press Club, which had entered its 6,408th day. According to TBP, Comrade Manzoor Baloch and Inqilab Communist Party leader Karim Parhad were among those who visited the protest camp. Participants demanded the recovery of missing persons and condemned their alleged extrajudicial killings. VBMP chairman Nasrullah Baloch said enforced disappearances and alleged extrajudicial killings violated the Constitution, the law and fundamental human rights, leaving affected families in prolonged distress. He urged the government to ensure the safe return of missing persons, stressing that anyone accused of an offence should be produced before a court and given an opportunity to defend themselves. Nasrullah also called for transparent investigations into the reported disappearances to identify those responsible and ensure accountability. He maintained that the issue should be resolved through constitutional, legal and democratic means rather than through the use of force. TBP further noted that enforced disappearances remain a longstanding concern in Balochistan, with families and human rights organisations repeatedly staging protests against alleged detentions at undisclosed locations and demanding that those held be produced before courts. Citing the Human Rights Council of Balochistan's (HRCB) September report, TBP said the organisation documented 54 enforced disappearances, including five cases from previous months. Among those reported missing were nine teenagers, two women and a young girl. The HRCB also recorded 11 reappearances and four deaths in custody during the reporting period, while most of those reported missing remained unaccounted for, the report added. (ANI)

item.title: "It's a brave new world": Elon Musk fires back as Democrat demands pause on advanced AI, ban on superintelligence
item.description: Elon Musk responded to Arizona Democratic Representative Yassamin Ansari's call for a pause on advanced AI development, stricter industry regulation, and a ban on artificial superintelligence by ...
item.content:encoded:
"It's a brave new world": Elon Musk fires back as Democrat demands pause on advanced AI, ban on superintelligence Elon Musk responded to Arizona Democratic Representative Yassamin Ansari's call for a pause on advanced AI development, stricter industry regulation, and a ban on artificial superintelligence by posting on X, "It's a Brave New World." ANI | Updated: 05-11-2026 14:02 IST | Created: 05-11-2026 14:02 IST

Space X CEO Elon Musk (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has reacted to a recent policy call by Arizona Democratic Representative Yassamin Ansari regarding the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence. In a post on X, Musk wrote, "It's a Brave New World". The entrepreneur's commentary followed a statement shared by Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari on the platform, in which she argued that regulating the sector should be an immediate priority. "Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out-of-control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence," Ansari wrote. This friction over technological policy unfolds against a broader backdrop of political upheaval, as Musk separately reacted to sweeping Democratic victories in the 2026 US midterm elections with sarcastic posts on X, including a remark that "data centres in space" were looking increasingly appealing, after Republicans suffered major electoral setbacks despite his extensive financial support for their campaigns. In two separate posts on X, Musk first quipped, "Data centres in space looking pretty appealing right now," before adding, "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time." The remarks came after Democrats made significant gains in the midterm elections, with US networks projecting that the party would reclaim control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, marking a major reversal in the balance of power in Washington. Musk, the world's richest man, had emerged as one of the biggest financial supporters of Republican candidates during the election cycle, spending approximately USD 250 million to assist the party's congressional campaigns, according to NBC News. One of his biggest political investments was in the Texas Senate contest, where Republican candidate Ken Paxton lost to Democrat James Talarico, marking a significant Democratic breakthrough in a traditionally Republican stronghold. Talarico also referred to Musk during his victory speech, drawing a comparison between his campaign and the biblical story of David taking on Goliath. He described Musk, along with President Donald Trump and the Washington, DC, establishment, as part of the powerful forces his campaign had challenged. Musk's comments regarding both AI regulation and space-based data centres also come amid growing political uncertainty surrounding the future of the technology sector following the Democratic gains, with stock futures falling overnight amid concerns over the implications for the industry. The Republican setback marks a particularly significant moment for Musk, whose heavy financial backing could not prevent high-profile defeats or stem Democrats' advances in traditionally conservative states. The election results have ultimately strengthened the Democrats' position in Congress, giving the party greater scope to challenge Trump's legislative agenda, intensify scrutiny of his administration during the remaining two years of his presidency, and push forward aggressive oversight of technology and artificial intelligence. (ANI)

item.title: Trump renews push for permanent daylight saving time, urges Senate to pass Sunshine Protection Act
item.description: US President Donald Trump urged the Senate to pass the Sunshine Protection Act to make daylight saving time permanent, criticising early winter sunsets and stalled bipartisan legislation in Congress.
item.content:encoded:
Trump renews push for permanent daylight saving time, urges Senate to pass Sunshine Protection Act US President Donald Trump urged the Senate to pass the Sunshine Protection Act to make daylight saving time permanent, criticising early winter sunsets and stalled bipartisan legislation in Congress. ANI | Updated: 05-11-2026 13:02 IST | Created: 05-11-2026 13:02 IST

US President Donald Trump (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump has strongly urged the Senate to clear the Sunshine Protection Act, voicing sharp frustration over early evening darkness in a recent social media statement. Taking to Truth Social, the US leader drew attention to the swift onset of dusk, noting that sunset occurred at 5:06 pm while total darkness had descended by 5:31 pm. "It's so dark outside, so early," he wrote, reflecting on the seasonal shift. The proposed legislation aims to establish daylight saving time permanently across the country, thereby halting the biannual ritual of adjusting clocks backwards and forwards. Reflecting on the public frustration surrounding time changes, Trump remarked, "Just a few days ago it was so nice and sunny at this same time," while adding that citizens had been "running around changing their clocks all over the place". The President highlighted that the House of Representatives has repeatedly endorsed the bill with substantial bipartisan backing, citing a decisive vote of 308-117, whereas the upper chamber has consistently stalled consideration. "The House sent it over to the Senate with great bipartisan support, numerous times (308-117), but the Senate didn't take it up," Trump stated. Furthermore, the President noted that he deliberately refrained from elevating the matter into a prominent campaign issue prior to the recent electoral cycle, explaining that he wished to shield vulnerable lawmakers from severe electoral backlash. "We have far bigger priorities, but I will keep fighting for this!" he asserted. The lower chamber originally advanced the measure in July, transmitting the text to the Senate, where it has encountered legislative resistance. (ANI)
